# Plugin CLI and generated files reference

`@veap/plugins` and `@veap/database` integrate with the `veap` console runner to manage installed plugins, regenerate static bundler registries (`lib/plugins.gen.ts`), scaffold database migrations (`migrations/index.ts`), and eject npm plugins into local workspace packages (`plugins/<name>`).

## CLI commands for plugins and migrations

Run these commands from your application root using `bun veap <command>`:

| Command | Package | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `veap list-plugins` | `@veap/plugins` | Lists all plugins registered in the application along with their version and enabled state. |
| `veap add <package>` | `@veap/plugins` | Installs a plugin package (`--local`, `--skip-install`), prompts for required `.env` variables, installs `veap.dependencies`, and regenerates `lib/plugins.gen.ts`. |
| `veap remove <package>` | `@veap/plugins` | Uninstalls a plugin package (`--skip-install`) and removes its import from `lib/plugins.gen.ts`. |
| `veap eject <package>` | `@veap/plugins` | Clones the plugin's source repository into `plugins/<name>`, configures `"workspaces": ["plugins/*"]` in `package.json`, pins the dependency to `"workspace:*"`, links it via your package manager, and regenerates `lib/plugins.gen.ts`. |
| `veap make:plugin <name>` | `@veap/plugins` | Scaffolds a new local plugin in `plugins/<name>-plugin` (`--dir`, `--skip-register`), registers it as `"workspace:*"` in `package.json`, and regenerates `lib/plugins.gen.ts`. |
| `veap plugins:sync` | `@veap/plugins` | Scans `package.json` for installed Veap plugins and regenerates `lib/plugins.gen.ts`. |
| `veap make:migration <name>` | `@veap/database` | Creates a new timestamped migration file in `migrations/` and exports it from `migrations/index.ts`. |
| `veap migrate` | `@veap/database` | Applies all pending application and plugin migrations. |
| `veap migrate:status` | `@veap/database` | Prints the status and batch number of every registered migration. |
| `veap migrate:rollback` | `@veap/database` | Rolls back the most recent migration batch (`--force` bypasses interactive confirmation). |

## Generated project files

Two files in a Veap application are maintained automatically by CLI tooling so Next.js and Turbopack can statically analyze imports without dynamic `fs` scanning at runtime:

### `lib/plugins.gen.ts`

Generated and updated by `veap add`, `veap remove`, `veap eject`, `veap make:plugin`, and `veap plugins:sync`. It statically imports every installed plugin and exports the `plugins: IPlugin[]` array consumed by `lib/veap.ts`:

```ts
// Auto-generated by @veap/plugins CLI — do not edit manually
import type { IPlugin } from "@veap/plugins";
import blogPlugin from "@veap/blog-plugin";

export const plugins: IPlugin[] = [blogPlugin];
```

### `migrations/index.ts`

Aggregates your host application's reversible migration definitions into the `appMigrations` array passed to `.withMigrations(appMigrations)` in `lib/veap.ts`:

```ts
import { createArticlesMigration } from "./20261001_create_articles";

export const appMigrations = [createArticlesMigration];
```

## How `veap eject` transitions ownership

When you run `bun veap eject @veap/blog-plugin`, the CLI performs five deterministic steps:

1. Clones the plugin's git repository into `plugins/blog-plugin`.
2. Adds `"plugins/*"` to the `workspaces` array in your root `package.json`.
3. Rewrites the dependency in `package.json` to `"@veap/blog-plugin": "workspace:*"`.
4. Runs your package manager's install step so `node_modules/@veap/blog-plugin` symlinks to `plugins/blog-plugin`.
5. Regenerates `lib/plugins.gen.ts`.

Because the package specifier (`@veap/blog-plugin`) stays identical while its resolution moves to your local `plugins/blog-plugin` workspace folder, your application code requires zero import changes and you gain full edit ownership over the plugin's components, routes, and models.
